capex prepares to surge from $154B in 2023 to over $1.3T by 2028, Pasquariello argued that evaluating AI investments in binary ROIC terms is overly reductive.

Drawing parallels to early enterprise cloud migration and compulsory cybersecurity spending, he outlined a broader framework: AI generates value by enabling companies to operate better, while also functioning as mandatory defensive spending to protect existing operations from disruption.

Because adoption is in its early stages, calculating precise financial returns is nearly impossible, Pasquariello wrote in a note. Furthermore, Goldman partner George Lee highlights that intense competitive pressures may redirect financial returns into consumer surplus rather than corporate balance sheets, Pasquariello added. Consequently, corporate America has clear justification to maintain high capex even when direct ROI is low or difficult to quantify.

Looking ahead, Pasquariello affirmed that the secular trend of AI investment remains intact but warned investors to prepare for a more jagged path.
